messages:
Tess: hey team :wave: I'm day 2 on eng-runtime. trying to build the runtime from source on an ubuntu 22.04 VM with CUDA 13.1 and driver 535.113. cmake + make fails at link time with lots of undefined refs to cuInit / cuDeviceGet. any quick ideas on where to start?
Mika: welcome! :tada: first guess: driver vs toolkit mismatch. can you paste `nvidia-smi` + the linker error (just the last ~10 lines)?
Tess: sure — here's nvidia-smi output and the tail of the link step:
```
$ nvidia-smi
Tue Mar  2 12:34:56 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.113       Driver Version: 535.113       CUDA Version: 13.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/liblibruntime.a(cuda_driver.o): in function `InitDriver':
cuda_driver.cpp:(.text+0x1a7): undefined reference to `cuInit'
cuda_driver.cpp:(.text+0x1d0): undefined reference to `cuDeviceGet'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Tess: also `ldd build/bin/runtime` shows `libcuda.so.1 => not found`
Samir: ok that explains it — libcuda should be provided by the driver (usually in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu). If `ldd` says not found then the dynamic linker can't see the driver library. Did you install the driver from distro package or via the runfile?
Tess: I ran the cuda runfile for the toolkit and skipped the bundled driver (I thought driver was already installed via apt).
Rosie: with runfile installs it's common to end up with the toolkit in /usr/local/cuda-13 and the driver libs not on the system loader path. Two quick fixes: (1) add `/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64` to /etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf and run `sudo ldconfig`, or (2) create a symlink from the driver-provided libcuda into the cuda toolchain lib dir — but prefer ldconfig approach.
Samir: also verify the driver actually installed the lib: `ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda*` — if that file exists, LD config is the issue. If it doesn't, you need the driver package (e.g., nvidia-driver-535) installed.
Tess: running the ls now:
```
$ ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda*
ls: cannot access '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda*': No such file or directory
```
Tess: so it's missing. I have `/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64/libcuda.so.1` though (from the toolkit runfile).
Mika: aha — libcuda from the toolkit is not the real driver lib in many cases. The kernel driver provides the real libcuda. Since `nvidia-smi` showed driver 535.113 you probably installed the driver elsewhere or it's out of sync. Try `dpkg -l | grep nvidia` or check the distro package.
Samir: if you want a quick local workaround to get your build linking, you can add `/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64` to your linker path during build: `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `cmake -DCMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64 ..` but long term install the proper driver package and run ldconfig.
Rosie: note: don't copy random libcuda.so from toolkit into /usr/lib — that'll create subtle ABI mismatches. prefer the driver package.
Tess: thanks. I installed `nvidia-driver-535` via apt and then did `sudo ldconfig`. now `ldd build/bin/runtime` shows `libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1`.
Tess: re-ran `make` and now hit a different error: `ptxas: error: /usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas: not found` during nvcc steps. weird because /usr/local/cuda-13/bin is in PATH.
Samir: is ptxas executable present? `ls -l /usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas` ? sometimes the runfile leaves it out depending on components selected.
Tess: `ls -l` shows the file is there but it's a 32-bit ELF that can't be executed on this VM? here's the file info:
```
$ file /usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas
/usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas: ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, 
```
Tess: hmm that looks fine. error message was from a build script wrapper that checks ptxas by running it. It fails with `Illegal instruction` on execution.
Mika: that often means the ptxas binary was built with newer cpu flags (e.g., AVX512) that VM doesn't support. Two options: use a matching container/host with proper CPU, or install the 
```
